acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Amy Roberts thought it was obvious that she was an adult, not a kid, and she assumed the friendly man working at the children's museum knew it too. Unfortunately, the man had Amy pegged all wrong. And by the time she figured it out, it was too late for either of them to save face. Host Ira Glass talks to Amy about the embarrassing ordeal that taught her never to assume she knows what someone else is thinking.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: While riding in a patrol car to research a novel, crime writer Richard Price witnessed a misunderstanding that, for many people, is pretty much accepted as an upsetting fact of life. Richard Price told this story, which he describes as a tale taken from real life and dramatized, onstage at The Moth in New York.
acts.title: The Fat Blue Line

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: There are situations where making judgments about people based on limited information is not only accepted but required. One of those situations is open adoption, where birth mothers actually choose the adoptive parents for their child. Producer Nancy Updike talks to a pregnant woman named Kim, going through the first stage of open adoption: reading dozens of letters from prospective parents, all of whom seem utterly capable and appealing.
acts.title: Yes, No or Baby

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: David Rakoff picks a fight with a hit Broadway show.
acts.title: Isn’t It Romantic?

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Shalom Auslander tells the story of the time he went on vacation, pegged the guest in the room next door as an imposter, and devoted his holiday to trying to prove it. Shalom is the author of Feh: a Memoir.

songs.t: Be Careful of the Stones You Throw

acts.title: Paradise Lost
